newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB says got no offers in Tractebel bid.
newsitem.headline: SGB says got no offers in Tractebel bid.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique said on Tuesday its 14,500 francs-a-share price maintenance operation on shares in Tractebel did not lead to any demand from Tractebel investors to sell their holdings.
"No shares were offered for sale while the share price maintenance operation...was in force from October 9 to 30, 1996," SGB said in a statement.
SGB said the result of the operation demonstrated the success of its concurrent offer of a free put warrant to Tractebel investors, giving them the right to sell at the same price in November 1999.
"These put warrants...will be listed separately on the stock market from November 15 onwards," SGB said.

SGB, which is 63 percent owned by France's Cie. de Suez, launched the price maintenance operation after acquiring a 24.47 percent stake in Tractebel from companies linked to Belgium's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
